analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation: one new row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 329) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. It describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. A 128-token shader-cache probe runs twice, and only a cold cache runs the shape cells, capped at 20 seconds per engine. It trains no rate or counter and is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No source code, key handling, wire contract, attestation, authorization, or cache storage logic is changed in the supplied evidence.

I examined the base text around lines 312-597 against the threat model. The related surfaces are T-041 (prefix cache and TTFT oracle), TB-007 (inference engine) and T-010/T-029 (availability). The new variable is described as warmup only, using synthetic probe shapes. It does not mention consumer prompts, the cache scope, the SSD tier, the TTL or encryption. I found no documented change to the A-001 exposure or to the T-041 mitigations.

Open questions for later review of the real implementation, which is not in this batch. First, the LaunchAgent passthrough means an operator-environment value is persisted into the daemon. This matters only if the code reads it without the stated validation. Second, the warmup runs at load time inside the 20-second per-engine cap. Third, 'always skips the probe', so the warmup would run on every load. Whether warmup uses real consumer data or touches the prefix cache cannot be confirmed from the doc row. Since the doc says it trains nothing and uses a synthetic shape, no concrete regression is evidenced. A documentation-only change cannot show that the implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) behaves safely. No findings.
